sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球供应链制造母港、跨境电商货源地与外资合规准入市场

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Visual Web Template and Low-Code Web Application Builder

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (codified; German/Japanese-influenced company law under the ROC legal order, with special administrative licensing regime for mainland-China investors)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Cross-Strait Economic Cooperation Framework Agreement (ECFA), signed 29 June 2010, in force 12 September 2010
Cross-Strait Agreement on Investment Protection and Promotion (海峽兩岸投資保障和促進協議), signed 9 August 2012, in force 1 February 2013
No PRC–Taiwan DTAA in force: Cross-Strait Tax Agreement signed 25 August 2015 remains unratified

stage_2.jurisdiction_and_entity_form_caveat: The payload identifies Taiwan (TW) as the jurisdiction but specifies a China WFOE entity form. A mainland-China WFOE cannot be incorporated under Taiwan law. This dossier addresses formation in Taiwan as a Taiwan company with foreign investment; it does not establish a mainland-China WFOE. Confirm the intended jurisdiction and legal form before filing.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act, including Articles 1, 18, 20, 156, 163, 170, 192, and 208, as applicable to the selected company form; Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals, including its foreign-investment approval requirements. Requirements depend on whether the investor chooses a company limited by shares or a company limited by shares with a single corporate shareholder.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce, or the competent local government business-registration authority under the applicable delegation; foreign investment approval is handled by the Investment Review Department, Ministry of Economic Affairs.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Registration Application (公司登記申請書), together with any required foreign investment approval application and supporting incorporation documents.
incorporation_legal_framework.official_state_filing_fee_note: Taiwan's company registration fee is assessed in New Taiwan dollars by reference to authorized capital, subject to statutory minimums and applicable online-filing reductions. There is no single fixed USD filing fee; the numeric field is not a representation that registration is free.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No general statutory minimum capital applies to an ordinary software company, subject to any sector-specific rule or visa/work-permit requirement. Capital must be sufficient for the proposed business. Foreign investment approval and foreign-exchange remittance procedures apply where relevant; capital is remitted through an authorized bank to the company's account and is subject to CPA verification where required. No general statutory escrow requirement applies.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company accept the subscriptions for the shares set out in the approved subscription documents, subject to receipt of the subscription funds and completion of applicable foreign-investment and registration procedures. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office stated in the approved incorporation documents is adopted as the Company's registered office. FURTHER RESOLVED, that [name] is appointed Chairperson, [name] is appointed General Manager, and [name] is authorized to execute and submit incorporation, tax, banking, and licensing filings on the Company's behalf. The officers shall maintain statutory books and records and report material compliance matters to the Board.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm jurisdiction, company form, and foreign-investment eligibility
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Review Department, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), and the competent company-registration authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm that Taiwan, rather than mainland China, is the intended place of incorporation. Select a Taiwan company form and check the current negative list, foreign-investment restrictions, and any sector-specific conditions for the proposed software activities. Obtain foreign-investment approval before investment where required. Foreign-language documents should be accompanied by Chinese translations; notarization or authentication may be required for overseas corporate and personal documents.
required_dossiers: Investor identification and ownership chart
Constitutional documents and good-standing evidence for corporate investors
Board or shareholder authorization for the investment
Proposed company name, business scope, capital, and shareholder structure
Chinese translations and applicable notarization or authentication
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to an information request within the stated deadline, provide corrected translations or authentication, and amend the investment proposal or ownership structure if the authority identifies a restriction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve company name and business scope
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MOEA online Company and Business Name Pre-check platform or the competent local government business-registration counter
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit proposed Chinese company names and the planned business items for pre-check. Use descriptions that accurately cover software development and website-builder services; do not claim regulated telecommunications, financial, or other licensed activities unless actually intended. Name pre-check is not incorporation.
required_dossiers: Name-precheck application
Proposed Chinese company names
Proposed business items and applicant identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Submit alternative names or revise business-item wording if a name is unavailable or an item is restricted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete foreign-investment approval and remit capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Review Department, MOEA; authorized foreign-exchange bank in Taiwan
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the foreign-investment application when required and obtain approval before remittance. Remit subscribed capital through an authorized bank using the approved investor and transaction details. Retain bank remittance and exchange-conversion records. Have a Taiwan CPA verify capital where required before company registration or subsequent amendment filing.
required_dossiers: Foreign-investment application and approval documents, if applicable
Investor source-of-funds and remittance information requested by the bank
Share subscription and capital payment records
Bank remittance certificates and CPA capital verification report, if required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct remittance references or investor details through the bank and investment authority; provide source-of-funds evidence or supplementary approval documents if requested.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt constitutional documents and appoint directors and officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company's incorporator, shareholders, and initial board; filings submitted to the competent company-registration authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and execute the articles of incorporation and incorporation resolutions in the required form and language. Appoint directors and any required supervisor or audit committee under the selected company form. Obtain written consents to act. Ensure overseas signatures and corporate authorizations meet applicable notarization, authentication, and translation requirements.
required_dossiers: Articles of incorporation
Incorporation minutes or written resolutions
Director and supervisor consents and identification
Registered-office consent or occupancy evidence
Share subscription schedule and capital evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct execution defects, provide missing consents or authenticated documents, and re-adopt resolutions if the registration authority requires changes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MOEA Department of Commerce or the competent local government company-registration authority, using its company-registration e-filing system or counter
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Company Registration Application and supporting documents after satisfying applicable investment and capital procedures. Pay the fee assessed in New Taiwan dollars. Use the registered office and business items approved at name pre-check. Keep the filing receipt and promptly monitor the portal or correspondence for deficiencies.
required_dossiers: Company Registration Application
Approved articles and incorporation resolutions
Foreign-investment approval, if applicable
Director and officer information and consents
Registered-office evidence
Capital evidence and CPA report, if required
Name-precheck result and fee payment proof
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: File supplementary materials or corrected forms by the response deadline. If rejected, review the written grounds, cure the stated defect, and refile or use the available administrative appeal procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete tax registration and establish operational records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau responsible for the registered-office location; authorized bank for account opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After company registration, complete tax and business-registration procedures, obtain the tax identification number, and apply for any required uniform invoice or e-invoice setup. Open the corporate bank account and maintain accounting books, shareholder records, beneficial ownership information, and corporate seals in accordance with applicable law.
required_dossiers: Company registration certificate and approved registration particulars
Articles and authorized signatory records
Registered-office evidence
Tax registration forms and business-item information
Beneficial ownership and bank due-diligence materials
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct tax-registration details, provide additional premises or beneficial-owner evidence, and complete any requested tax-office inspection or interview.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial licensing board is ordinarily applicable to a software-only website-builder business in Taiwan. The competent company-registration authority is the MOEA Department of Commerce or delegated local government; separate approvals may apply if actual activities include regulated services.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No general manufacturing or industrial operating license is ordinarily required for software development and online website-builder services. Separate permissions may be required for regulated telecommunications, financial, or other controlled activities.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Administration, Executive Yuan (now the Ministry of Environment)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Ordinarily exempt from project-level EIA for a software-only office operation that is not a listed development project or designated facility.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No manufacturing wastewater, process VOC, or industrial-waste thresholds are ordinarily triggered by software-only office operations. Comply with applicable municipal sewer, air-pollution, noise, and waste rules if the premises or actual activities trigger them; use licensed waste handlers where required.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No manufacturing-site clearance is ordinarily required for a software office. The building must have lawful occupancy and comply with applicable building-use, fire-safety, and workplace requirements. Fire inspection or equipment certification may be required depending on building use, floor area, occupancy, and local fire authority rules; structural-load review is relevant only where premises alterations or equipment loads warrant it. Register and comply with applicable occupational safety requirements.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) jointly with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE); SAFE is the operational regulator for cross-border receipts, payments, and capital-account conversion.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Chinese renminbi (RMB) is fully convertible for current-account items, including trade-in-goods and trade-in-services, subject to authentic documentation and bank-level verification. Capital-account convertibility remains restricted; foreign direct investment (FDI) capital inflows, profit repatriation, and shareholder loans require SAFE registration, bank confirmation, and post-event monitoring. For the WFOE, dividend remittance to the Taiwan shareholder is treated as a capital-account outflow, but it is routinely permitted when: (i) audited financial statements are filed; (ii) corporate income tax on the distributed retained earnings has been settled and the tax clearance/proof is retained; (iii) an SAFE foreign-exchange payment declaration is executed at the designated bank; and (iv) the bank can evidence a genuine in-country profit base. The principal practical hurdle is not unlawful or scarce FX quota, but the need for a flawless documentary chain: audited accounts, the board resolution approving distribution, the WFOE's seal/certificate of good standing, and the shareholder's tax-residency paperwork.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For a Chinese WFOE exporting software-as-a-service or digitally delivered services, export earnings must flow back into a domestic current-account foreign-exchange settlement account under SAFE's total-amount verification framework. The statutory orientation period is typically within 90 days from the date of customs declaration or from the service-completion/proforma-declaration date, depending on the applicable trade category; any delay requires bank annotation and may trigger a total-amount verification warning. There is no mandatory surrender ratio for conversion into RMB: the WFOE may retain the foreign currency in the settlement account or convert wholesale/retail into RMB at the prevailing market rate, provided the underlying transaction is genuine, supported by contracts, service descriptions, invoices, and debit/credit sweeps in the bank's electronic monitoring platform.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of China – Corporate Banking Department (BOC)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (FDI capital account) + Operational Current Account (RMB and FCY settlement)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account + Operational Settlement Account
Capital Escrow Account + Businessecosystem Settlement Account with enhanced digital treasury dashboard
Capital Escrow Account + General Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a primary treasury host; Medium as a supplementary collection rail. Offshore digital EMI platforms such as Airwallex, Currenxie, and Payoneer are not licensed by PBOC or SAFE as depository institutions in mainland China. They cannot hold RMB client funds in a protected trust structure, cannot obtain SAFE onshore settlement codes, and cannot lawfully provide local payment acceptance for onshore contracts. However, an offshore EMI can act as a downstream recipient of the WFOE's outbound trade proceeds or WA provider invoice collection from overseas customers, provided all RMB settlements for mainland activity continue to be collected through a licensed Chinese bank or an approved cross-border RMB payment institution (e.g., licensed non-bank institutions under PBOC's 2019 cross-border payment pilot). The legality constraint is satisfied only if the WFOE's invoicing and contract flow designate the EMI as a global payment facilitation channel, not as a domestic account holder.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory for first-time corporate account opening at a Chinese commercial bank. The legal representative or at least one board director with controlling authority, together with the designated authorized signatory and the company controller/ultimate beneficial owner (if different), must appear in person at the bank's counter for a KYC interview, sealing of account documents, and said compliance interview with the relationship manager. Remote/online onboarding for a foreign-owned mainland WFOE is not generally permitted; some pilot Free Trade Zone Branches, especially in Shanghai, Hainan, and Qianhai, allow a hybrid process, but a physical appearance is still required for the production of the 'FDI Confirmation Form' and activation of the capital escrow account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Overseas shareholder resides in Taiwan and there is a company cross-border structure without an immediate mainland tax identification document for the shareholder.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the Taiwan shareholder's corporate registration certificate, board resolution opening the WFOE, the WFOE's business license evidencing FDI approval by MOFCOM/SAMR, the SAFE FDI registration certificate, tax-residence certificates of the shareholder, and a detailed source-of-wealth narrative with six months of bank statements in the shareholder's name.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The WFOE conducts a purely digital SaaS business with no physical office inventory or obvious business assets.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply SaaS platform documentation, software code repository ownership, domain registration records, customer contracts and/or licensing agreements, IP assignments, trademark filings, and audited financial statements or CPA-reviewed management accounts showing genuine software development activity and commercial revenue volumes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Revenue is collected via third-party payment processors (Stripe, Paddle), which may indicate a booking center model or hidden intermediary.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the valid Merchant Services Agreement with Stripe/Paddle, the WFOE's board approval designating those processors, reconciliation reports tracing settlement balances back to invoice numbers, customer purchase invoices, and an explanation of the payment-flow relationship demonstrating that providers remit the net proceeds directly to the WFOE's onshore bank account in compliance with PBOC/SAFE.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound payments to foreign contractors or licensing payments to a Taiwan group entity create a red flag of thin capitalization or round-tripping.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare a transfer-pricing file (based on the OECD Guidelines and China's BR 42 Beneficial Ownership and BEPS), service agreements with detailed deliverables, board minutes authorizing the payments, an executed loan or IP license agreement with appropriate registration, and an independent valuation report if the payment is for intangible assets or intercompany charges.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Taiwan parent (or ultimate foreign investor) initiates an SWIFT MT103 payment from its Taiwanese bank to the WFOE's capital escrow account with the designated mainland bank. The remittance instruction must reference: (a) the SAFE/FDI registration number issued to the WFOE; (b) the bank-issful 'FDI Business Confirmation Form' reference; and (c) the explicit transaction purpose code for foreign direct investment equity injection (SAFE code category 6, typically 621 or 622 as directed by the bank's FX officer). The receiving bank will perform a 'capital-account payment verification', convert the foreign currency into RMB on the WFOE's instruction (or maintain a foreign-currency capital balance), and restrict the use of funds to the WFOE's actual operational scope, facilities, payroll, software development, and overhead, subject to a negative list prohibiting securities investment and non-business real-estate speculation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For operating disbursements (software contractor payments, cloud infrastructure costs, international licensing fees, and offshore distribution fees), the WFOE will purchase foreign currency from its local settlement bank against the RMB operational account and execute an SWIFT MT103 with the relevant SAFE service/trade purpose code; a copy of the contract, invoice, tax payment certificate (if required), and any withholding tax voucher are attached via the bank's electronic single-window. For high-value procurement of infrastructure hardware or a mission-critical code asset, the WFOE may use a commercial documentary letter of credit (L/C) issued by the mainland bank in favor of the overseas beneficiary; the L/C will be settled via SWIFT MT700 with the negotiating bank, and the WFOE must align the underlying contract documents, Bill of Lading/Air Waybill or electronic delivery receipt, and the commercial invoice. For recurring royalties or SaaS licensing fees, an FX payment instruction plus a withholding tax documentation package is the standard rail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore trade-backed forward foreign-exchange contract between the WFOE and its designated settlement bank (CNY/USD or CNY/TWD forward) to hedge a committed USD/TWD revenue stream from international subscribers.

FX swap (spot vs. forward) with a licensed Chinese bank, with the underlying being a genuine current-account transaction or a scheduled capital-account conversion; the hedge is settled by actual delivery, not by netting.
Cross-currency interest-rate swap permitted only where there is an actual foreign-currency debt or investment exposure (e.g., an overseas loan raised for software licensing acquisition).
Plain-vanilla FX options (call/put on CNY or foreign currency) under SAFE's actual-exposure requirement, provided the bank's internal compliance clears the hedge for documentation and tenor.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Settlement Return including Undistributed Surplus Tax schedule (營利事業所得稅結算申報暨未分配盈餘申報)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance (財政部各地區國稅局)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by May 31 for the preceding fiscal year; CPA-assist extension to June 30 available for qualified filers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 3% of tax due per 2-day delay (max 30 days) and 0.5% per 2 days thereafter (total capped at 7.5%), with NT$1,500 minimum and NT$150,000 maximum; deferred tax accrues monthly interest at 1% per 3-day block; prolonged non-filing permits deemed assessment and may trigger dissolution/removal from the commercial register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Business Report, Financial Statements, and Profit Distribution / Loss Absorption Proposal approved by shareholders (有限公司: shareholder written consent per Company Act Art. 110)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate act; documentation retained at registered office and submitted to the Investment Commission (see separate item); no direct MOEA filing for a private limited company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by June 30 (six months from December 31 fiscal year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors failing to prepare or obtain shareholder consent face MOEA administrative fines of NT$10,000–NT$50,000 per Company Act Art. 20/110; continued breach beyond the next fiscal year-end risks compulsory dissolution and de-registration under Art. 10.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership and Significant-Shareholder Declaration (公司資訊暨實質受益人年度申報) covering directors, managers, and shareholders holding ≥10% of paid-in capital
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs – central company registration information platform (經濟部公司登記資料平台)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the MOEA-published reporting cycle (registration anniversary based); any change within 15 days via updated filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines of NT$10,000–NT$50,000 per violation under Company Act Art. 22-1; refusal to file blocks future MOEA registration services, increases AML/CFT regulator scrutiny, and may lead to dissolution for persistent non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report of Foreign-Invested Company (Business Report, CPA-certified or reviewed Financial Statements, and Profit Distribution Table) submitted by the invested company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (經濟部投資審議委員會)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within one month after shareholder consent to financial statements; hard annual deadline July 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing suspends Investment Commission processing of capital increases, share transfers, dividend remittance, and name/scope amendments; willful default can trigger revocation of the investment approval and compelled disinvestment of the WFOE.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory CPA audit when paid-in capital reaches NT$30 million or more; also required for all companies whose sectoral licensing demands audited statements, and in practice by the Investment Commission and external financing covenants for the annual report of a foreign-invested enterprise; micro WFOEs below the capital threshold are exempt from compulsory external audit but must still keep proper accounts under the Business Entity Accounting Act.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Business Entity Accounting Act (商業會計法) and its Handling Standards; Taiwan Enterprise Accounting Standards (EAS) issued by the ARDF and endorsed by the FSC for non-public entities; IFRS not compulsory for non-public WFOEs; taxable income is computed through a separate tax-adjustment reconciliation on the Corporate Income Tax Settlement Return.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Company Act Art. 22-1 requires the WFOE to file an annual electronic declaration of ultimate beneficial owners and holders of ≥10% of contributed capital, directors, and managers with the MOEA platform; any shareholding transfer or BO change must be re-reported within 15 days, which supersedes the annual cycle; for mainland-China-connected investors, the Investment Commission's cross-strait approval terms require that the annual report state unchanged ownership, and any share transfer requires prior Investment Commission permission.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (股東名簿) – maintained at registered office showing name, nationality, contribution amount, voting rights, and transfer history
Register of Directors (董事名冊) – filed with MOEA and kept on site identifying the managing director(s) and their representative powers
Minute Book (議事錄暨股東同意書) – records of shareholders' written consents, board/executive resolutions, and the annual approval of financial statements

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 – 1,500 per year for registered business address and corporate secretarial/registered-agent services in Taipei, Taichung, or Kaohsiung
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000 – 5,000 per engagement when a CPA audit is mandatory or requested for Investment Commission/bank purposes; zero when not required below the NT$30 million threshold

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small low-profit enterprise concession: effective 5% on taxable income up to RMB 3,000,000 where employees do not exceed 300 and total assets do not exceed RMB 50,000,000 (20% reduced rate applied with an additional 25% tax-base reduction). High and New Technology Enterprise: 15%. National key-encouraged software enterprise: 10%. R&D super-deduction: 200% of eligible software product R&D expenditure deductible. Foreign-invested no-code builder may combine the small-enterprise rate with the R&D super-deduction if quantitative tests are met.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: 中华人民共和国企业所得税月（季）度预缴纳税申报表（A类）— Quarterly Provisional Corporate Income Tax Return (A-Class), Forms A200000/A201000 series, filed through the State Taxation Administration Electronic Tax Bureau (电子税务局, etax.chinatax.gov.cn).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 15 calendar days after the end of each calendar quarter (April 15, July 15, October 15, and January 15 following the Q4 period-end).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cumulative operating revenue for the current year (SaaS subscription billings, Stripe/Paddle remittances net of refunds, and other software service revenue).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report in RMB; foreign-currency revenue converted at the PBOC central parity rate on the last day of the filing quarter; reconcile with bank receipts before remittance of dividends.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cumulative operating cost (server hosting, cloud infrastructure, third-party developer labor, amortization of capitalized software development).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Costs paid to Taiwan or other non-resident related parties must be priced at arm's length and supported by contemporaneous documentation to avoid disallowance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cumulative accounting total profit (operating profit plus non-operating income less non-operating expenses).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconciliation with the audited Chinese CPA financial statements is expected; deviations flagged by the tax bureau require explanation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Actual profit used for prepayment (accounting profit adjusted for specified timing differences).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No credit is given for any deemed foreign tax credit at prepayment stage; full reconciliation occurs on the annual return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prepayable enterprise income tax computed at 25% on Line 6 actual profit, net of cumulative prior prepayments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Taiwan parent provides management services invoiced to the WFOE, their deductibility must be verified before including in the prepayment base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Preferential tax reduction (small-enterprise effective 5% rate, HNTEC 15% rate, or software-enterprise 10% rate).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Preferences are self-assessed; supporting qualification certificates and contemporaneous records must be kept for the 10-year retention period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Current-period tax due or refund after applying cumulative prepaid amounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where the refund arises from treaty relief on prior withholding, the tax bureau may require treaty-benefit information reports before release.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: fixed fine of RMB 2,000, increased to RMB 2,000–10,000 where circumstances are serious, under Article 62 of the Tax Administration and Collection Law. Late payment: daily surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid amount under Article 32 TACL, accruing from the statutory deadline until full settlement; the tax authority may also compel filing and freeze bank accounts.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: 中华人民共和国企业所得税年度纳税申报表（A类，2017年版） — Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (A-Class), main from A100000 with schedules A105000 (tax adjustment), A105080 (depreciation), A107010 (preferential), A108000 (foreign tax credit) and G100000-series related-party transaction schedules; filed through the same Electronic Tax Bureau portal and accompanied by the statutory Chinese CPA audit report.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 5 months after the fiscal year-end, in all cases by May 31 of the following year; annual reconciliation between quarterly prepayments and actual annual liability is completed on the same filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual operating revenue from the audited income statement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Wholly foreign-owned enterprise must file the statutory audit before submission; deferred revenue from annual software subscriptions recognized per ASC/PRC GAAP.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual operating cost, including capitalized software development amortization and cloud hosting overhead.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to Taiwan affiliates exceeding the service-transaction threshold must carry contemporaneous Local File documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting total profit before tax as audited.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must equal the audited profit after eliminating intercompany software license fees that have not met the beneficial-ownership substance test.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustment increases (non-deductible expenses, excess related-party management fees, non-arm's-length interest, entertainment expenses above caps).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Management fee allocations from the Taiwan parent exceeding 5% or lacking actual service evidence are added back.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustment decreases (R&D super-deduction, prior-year losses claimed, tax-exempt income).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: R&D super-deductions require a separate project ledger and contemporaneous technical documentation; foreign-funded R&D equally qualifies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual taxable income after all adjustments and loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss carryforward limited to 5 years for ordinary enterprises; losses of the WFOE cannot be shifted to the Taiwan parent.
Non-resident shareholders have no direct use of the entity's rate; withholding applies separately at distribution.
Ensure quarterly prepayments are not understated; underpayment triggers daily surcharge from the reconciliation deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax reduction and exemption (small-enterprise effective 5%, HNTEC, software enterprise).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Taiwan shareholder cannot independently invoke these reductions on the WFOE's return; entity-level qualification controls.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Actual annual tax payable after all exemptions and reductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any foreign tax credit is generally unavailable unless the WFOE has foreign branch/source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance of tax due or refund after offsetting quarterly prepayments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where a refund is to be applied against dividend WHT due to the Taiwan shareholder, the tax bureau coordinates the two settlements.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late annual filing: RMB 2,000–10,000 fine and compulsory filing order under Article 62 TACL; late payment: 0.05% daily surcharge; understatement due to false entries attracts the Article 63 penalty of 50%–500% of underpaid tax; failure to file related-party transaction schedules carries an RMB 2,000–10,000 penalty per schedule; tax officials may restrict export of profits until the return is accepted.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on the gross dividend paid by the China WFOE to its non-resident shareholder (CIT Law Article 3 and Article 37, withheld by the WFOE as withholding agent on the distribution date); rate may be reduced to 5% where the Taiwan corporate shareholder directly holds at least 25% of the WFOE's paid-in capital and the Cross-Strait tax arrangement relief is effectively available and evidenced.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Under STA Announcement [2019] No. 35, treaty benefit is claimed by self-assessment: the Taiwan shareholder files the 'Information Report on Enjoyment of Tax Treaty Benefits' through the e-Tax Bureau for each dividend distribution, attaches a Taiwan Tax Residence Certificate (税收居民身份证明) issued by the competent Taiwan tax authority, provides shareholding and beneficial-ownership declarations, and retains supporting records for 10 years. For the Cross-Strait Agreement on Avoidance of Double Taxation (signed 2015), relief is granted administratively only after reciprocal implementation; if not yet operational toward the specific Taiwan resident, the domestic 10% WHT applies. Withholding must be settled before the dividend is wired; the WFOE must obtain and keep the withholding certificate (扣缴企业所得税报告表).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory source WHT: 10% on gross interest and 10% on gross royalties paid by the China WFOE to a non-resident enterprise (statutory 20% rate reduced to 10%). Under the Cross-Strait arrangement: interest capped at 10% and royalties capped at 10%, with a lower rate only where specifically agreed. Software license and SaaS technology-right fees are generally characterized as royalties for WHT purposes unless transferred as bundled rights with substantial services; the Taiwan recipient must submit a TRC and substance evidence to invoke any treaty cap. Failure to withhold exposes the WFOE to a late-withholding penalty of 50%–300% of the unwithheld amount and full recovery interest.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Master File (主体文档) required where aggregate annual related-party transactions exceed RMB 1,000,000,000. Local File (本地文档) required where any one category exceeds: RMB 200,000,000 for tangible asset transfer; RMB 100,000,000 for intangible asset transfer; RMB 100,000,000 for financial asset transfer; RMB 40,000,000 for related-party service payments (annual paid amount). Annual related-party transaction reporting (G100000-series schedules) is mandatory whenever any related-party transaction exists, regardless of the documentation thresholds. Thresholds apply to the no-code builder's intercompany software-license, hosting, and management-fee flows with the Taiwan parent.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: PRC GAAR under CIT Law Article 47 and STA Order No. 32 (2015) recharacterizes arrangements lacking bona fide commercial substance. Beneficial-ownership relief under STA Announcement [2018] No. 9 requires substantive business operation, actual staff, premises, decision-making, and risk assumption in the claimant. A Taiwan parent that is a pure conduit or shell fails the substance test and will be denied the 5% dividend rate. For the ISIC 6201 no-code SaaS builder, economic substance is evidenced by local R&D engineers, Chinese cloud hosting contracts, customer acquisition and support operations, board minutes that govern pricing, and actual performance of development and maintenance services by the WFOE.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating SaaS subscription revenue, suppressing Stripe/Paddle remittances, overstating development costs, or recording fictitious staff and vendor payments to reduce the WFOE's taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 63 TACL: penalty of 50%–500% of the underpaid tax plus a daily 0.05% late surcharge; criminal prosecution under PRC Criminal Law Article 201 where evaded tax exceeds RMB 50,000 and exceeds 10% of tax payable, carrying up to 7 years' imprisonment and criminal fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative, chief financial officer and any director participating in the evasion face criminal liability as directly responsible persons; civil restitution of underpaid tax; tax authority may apply an exit ban (阻止出境) under Article 44 TACL until tax, penalties and surcharges are fully settled or security is provided.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Fraudulent Issuance or Procurement of Invoices (虚开发票)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing or obtaining false VAT special invoices for software development, marketing or consulting services not actually rendered, or using invoice-splitting to inflate costs and strip profit to the Taiwan side.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Invoice Management Measures, a fine up to RMB 500,000, disallowance of the inflated expense, denial of VAT input credits, and referral for criminal prosecution under Criminal Law Article 205, which provides up to life imprisonment and property confiscation for serious false-invoice rings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and financial controllers who authorize false invoicing are subject to criminal prosecution as principal offenders, personal fines, disqualification from corporate office in China, civil liability for unlawful gains to the company, and exit bans pending investigation and enforcement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation (关联交易定价不合规)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling no-code platform subscriptions or IP to the Taiwan parent below arm's length, paying inflated fees for offshore hosting or management services, or failing to file G100000-series related-party schedules and contemporaneous documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary tax adjustment plus interest computed at the PBOC benchmark lending rate plus 5 percentage points from June 1 of the affected tax year until payment; failure to maintain documentation triggers an RMB 2,000–10,000 fine and presumption of adjusted income; intentional mispricing may additionally attract a 50%–500% Article 63 penalty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors signing false transfer-pricing analyses face criminal liability for tax evasion where willfulness is proved; tax authorities may issue exit bans and property-preservation orders; the WFOE's legal representative may be required to give personal guarantees for the adjusted tax before profit repatriation is permitted.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Interposing a zero-substance Hong Kong, BVI or Cayman holding company above the WFOE solely to claim the reduced dividend withholding rate or to defer mainland recognition of the Taiwan ultimate owner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits under the beneficial-ownership test; recharacterization of the entire chain under GAAR (STA Order No. 32); supplementary assessment of tax at full 25% with interest computed on a compounded basis and no statute-of-limitations protection for abusive schemes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors of the shell and the WFOE legal representative who execute artificial arrangements are jointly liable for the additional tax; travel bans and freezing of personal bank accounts may be ordered; documented knowledge of the sham exposes directors to criminal liability for false treaty declarations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering and Illicit Cross-Border Payment Flows
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the WFOE's Stripe/Paddle merchant accounts to collect funds for undisclosed resellers, round-tripping subscription receipts with the Taiwan parent without commercial substance, or moving funds in cash-like layers to obscure beneficial ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the PRC Anti-Money Laundering Law: fines up to RMB 5,000,000 for the institution and up to RMB 500,000 for responsible persons; asset freezing; license revocation in egregious cases; criminal liability under Criminal Law Article 191 for money laundering, punishable by up to 10 years' imprisonment and criminal fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers and beneficial owners with knowledge of the laundering receive personal fines, confiscation of illicit proceeds, travel bans, and criminal prosecution; those who merely facilitate the flows face secondary liability for damages suffered by the WFOE and its lawful shareholders.
